questions.question: Which organisation has released the India Justice Report (IJR) in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tata Trusts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tata Trusts** is the primary organization responsible for releasing the **India Justice Report (IJR)**. The report was first launched in 2019 and continues to be an annual publication.
 
• The **India Justice Report** evaluates and ranks Indian states and Union Territories based on their ability to deliver justice through four pillars: **Police, Judiciary, Prisons, and Legal Aid.**
 
• The report is prepared in collaboration with other organizations such as **Centre for Social Justice, Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative (CHRI),** and **Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy,** among others.
 
• The objective of the report is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the justice delivery system in India, helping policymakers and citizens identify areas requiring improvement.
 
• The report utilizes various **quantitative and qualitative indicators**, including budgets, infrastructure, vacancies, diversity, and workload, to rank states and Union Territories.
 
• The **2025 edition** of the report, released in April, continues to highlight disparities in justice delivery across India, offering actionable insights for improved governance. *Hence, the correct option is Tata Trusts.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Tata Trusts:**

 
 
• **Tata Trusts** is one of the oldest philanthropic organizations in India, established in **1892** by **Jamsetji Tata.**
 
• The trust focuses on areas like **education, healthcare, rural development, and governance.** The **India Justice Report** is a part of its commitment to strengthening governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of India Justice Report:**
 
 
• The report ranks states based on their performance in **justice delivery.** States are categorized into large and small states for fair comparison.
 
• Indicators include **per capita expenditure on police and judiciary, representation of women, availability of legal aid lawyers, and prison occupancy rates.**
 
• The report aims to highlight gaps in justice delivery and encourage states to prioritize reforms in this domain.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Ambedkar Trusts:** Focuses on social justice and welfare activities, but it does not publish the India Justice Report.
 
• **National Trusts:** Primarily works on disability welfare and does not deal with justice reports.
 
• **Bombay Public Trusts:** Focuses on charitable and community welfare activities but is not involved in justice system assessments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the India Justice Report:**

 
 
• The report provides **data-driven insights** to help policymakers and stakeholders address challenges in justice delivery.
 
• It serves as a tool for **accountability** and encourages states to take corrective measures.
 
 
 
• **Key Findings of Previous Reports:**
 
 
• **Police:** Persistent vacancies, low representation of women, and inadequate training facilities.
 
• **Judiciary:** High pendency of cases and lack of adequate infrastructure and human resources.
 
• **Prisons:** Overcrowding and poor living conditions for inmates.
 
• **Legal Aid:** Limited access to legal aid services for marginalized communities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a national waterway between Haldia (Sagar) and Prayagraj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterways 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterways 1 (NW-1):** It is the waterway connecting **Haldia (Sagar) in West Bengal to Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh**. It is the **longest National Waterway in India**, spanning approximately **1,620 km**.
 
• NW-1 runs along the **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly River System**, making it a crucial route for inland water transport and trade.
 
• This waterway serves as an **economic lifeline** for the eastern and northern parts of India, facilitating efficient transportation of goods and passengers.
 
• The development and maintenance of NW-1 are overseen by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, which is responsible for ensuring smooth navigation.
 
• NW-1 is part of India’s initiative to **boost inland water transport** under the **Jal Marg Vikas Project**, supported by the **World Bank**.
 
• The route has multiple **terminals and infrastructure facilities**, such as Varanasi, Sahibganj, and Haldia, to enhance cargo handling capabilities.
 
• **Key commodities** transported along this waterway include fertilizers, coal, food grains, cement, and other industrial goods.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is National Waterways 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Waterways in India:**

 
 
• India has a total of **111 National Waterways**, covering major rivers, canals, and lakes across the country.
 
• They are developed to promote **inland water transport (IWT)** as a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative to road and rail transport.
 
 
 
• **Other National Waterways:**
 
 
• **National Waterway 2 (NW-2):** Runs along the **Brahmaputra River** in Assam from Dhubri to Sadiya, spanning approximately **891 km**.
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3):** Connects Kollam and Kottapuram along the **West Coast Canal** in Kerala, covering around **205 km**.
 
• **National Waterway 4 (NW-4):** Links the **Krishna and Godavari Rivers** in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, with a total length of **1,078 km**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Waterways:**
 
 
• Waterways reduce **congestion on roads** and lower transportation costs.
 
• They are **eco-friendly** and produce lower carbon emissions compared to road or rail transport.
 
• They enhance connectivity to **remote areas** and promote regional economic development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jal Marg Vikas Project:**

 
 
• This is a **Government of India initiative** to develop NW-1 from Haldia to Varanasi.
 
• It includes the construction of **multi-modal terminals, navigation locks**, and river information systems to enhance cargo movement.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges:**
 
 
• Waterways face challenges such as **seasonal water availability**, maintenance of dredging operations, and environmental concerns.
 
• Efficient use of waterways requires **adequate infrastructure**, including terminals, storage facilities, and navigational aids.

questions.question: Which organisation’s support was crucial in India’s globalisation process post 1991 economic crisis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IMF**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** played a crucial role in supporting India during the **1991 economic crisis**. This is the correct option as the IMF provided the necessary financial assistance to stabilize the Indian economy.
 
• In 1991, India faced a **balance of payments crisis**, with foreign exchange reserves falling to dangerously low levels, sufficient for only a few weeks of imports.
 
• The government approached the **IMF and the World Bank** for financial assistance. The IMF provided a loan of approximately **USD 2.2 billion** under the Structural Adjustment Program (SAP). This is a correct statement.
 
• The IMF's support was conditional upon implementing several economic reforms, including **liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG reforms)**, which led to significant changes in India's economic policies. Hence, the IMF's role was pivotal in India's globalization process post-1991.
 
• The reforms included the removal of trade barriers, reduction of import tariffs, and deregulation of industries to encourage foreign investment and competition, which were essential for India's globalization journey.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is IMF.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the IMF:**

 
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is an international financial institution headquartered in **Washington, D.C., United States**.
 
• It was established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference** and officially came into existence on **27 December 1945**.
 
• The IMF's primary purpose is to **ensure global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, facilitate international trade, promote high employment, and reduce poverty worldwide.**
 
 
 
• **India's Economic Crisis of 1991:**
 
 
• India faced a **severe economic crisis** in 1991 due to fiscal mismanagement, the Gulf War, and increasing oil prices, which depleted foreign exchange reserves.
 
• The reserves fell below **USD 1 billion**, barely enough to finance two weeks' worth of imports.
 
• To combat this crisis, the government pledged **67 tons of gold to the Bank of England** as collateral to secure a loan and approached the **IMF** for financial assistance.
 
 
 
• **LPG Reforms:**
 
 
• The IMF's loan was conditional on India implementing the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms.
 
• These reforms included:
 
 
• **Liberalization:** Reducing trade restrictions, import quotas, and tariff barriers.
 
• **Privatization:** Encouraging the private sector by reducing the dominance of public sector enterprises.
 
• **Globalization:** Opening up the economy to foreign direct investment (FDI) and promoting international trade.
 
 
 
• The reforms transformed India's economy, leading to high growth rates and integration into the global market.
 
 
 
• **Roles of Other Organizations:**
 
 
• **WHO:** The **World Health Organization (WHO)** focuses on global health issues and played no direct role in India’s economic reforms.
 
• **UNICEF:** The **United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)** works for child welfare and development but did not contribute to economic globalization in India.
 
• **UNESCO:** The **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)** focuses on education, science, and culture, unrelated to India's economic globalization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of IMF Support:**

 
 
• India's economy became more open and market-oriented, leading to increased foreign investment and higher GDP growth rates.
 
• The reforms laid the foundation for India to emerge as a major player in the global economy.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of 1991 Reforms:**
 
 
• The 1991 reforms are often seen as the beginning of **India's economic liberalization.**
 
• These reforms helped India transition from a tightly controlled economy to one with a significant global presence.

questions.question: Which district became the first in India to meet its entire power demand through solar energy, as of 2025?

• Through this initiative, Diu has significantly reduced its dependency on conventional power sources and has become a model for adopting **clean and renewable energy solutions**.
 
• This achievement was made possible due to the **government’s efforts to promote renewable energy**, in line with India’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions and combating climate change.
 
• The project has also helped the local population by bringing down electricity tariffs and providing a more **stable and sustainable power supply**.
 
• Diu’s transition to solar energy serves as an example of how small regions can take significant steps towards a **clean energy future** and contribute to environmental sustainability.

• Diu is a small district in the Union Territory of **Daman and Diu**, located on the western coast of India.

• **Solar Energy in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the world’s leading countries in **solar energy generation**, with ambitious targets under the **National Solar Mission**.
 
• As of 2023, India aims to achieve a capacity of **280 GW of solar power** by 2030.
 
• **Key initiatives** to promote solar energy include rooftop solar programs, solar parks, and subsidies for solar installations.
 
 
 
• **Other Districts Promoting Solar Energy:**

• The country has set a target of **500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity** by 2030.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Solar Energy:**
 
 
• Solar energy is a **clean, renewable, and sustainable source of power** that reduces dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• It helps in reducing **greenhouse gas emissions** and combating climate change.
 
• Solar energy systems have lower operational costs and can provide **energy security** to remote areas.

questions.question: When were Bahadur Shah Zafar and his wife Begum Zinat Mahal sent to prison in Rangoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**October 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, the last Mughal Emperor, was a symbolic figure during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**. He was proclaimed the leader by the rebels but lacked actual power or authority.
 
• After the British successfully suppressed the rebellion, Bahadur Shah Zafar was captured by the British forces in **September 1857**.
 
• He was tried in a military court for his role in the rebellion and charged with treason. The trial lasted for several months and culminated in his sentencing. *Hence, statement regarding his capture is correct.*
 
• In **October 1858**, Bahadur Shah Zafar, along with his wife **Begum Zinat Mahal** and some family members, was deported to **Rangoon (present-day Yangon, Myanmar)**.
 
• He lived the remainder of his life in exile in Rangoon, where he passed away in **November 1862**, marking the end of the Mughal dynasty. *Hence, the date October 1858 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar’s Role in the Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• Although **Bahadur Shah Zafar** was an aged and powerless ruler, the rebels declared him their leader during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• This was a symbolic move to unite Indians under the banner of the once-powerful Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Exile in Rangoon:**
 
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar’s exile was a part of the British strategy to eliminate any remnants of the Mughal Empire and assert their dominance.
 
• The British chose **Rangoon** as the place of exile to ensure that Zafar remained isolated and incapable of influencing Indian affairs.
 
• He spent the last four years of his life in Rangoon, dying in **1862**. His death marked the formal end of the Mughal dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Revolt:**
 
 
• The failure of the **1857 Revolt** led to significant changes in Indian administration, including the transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown in **1858**.
 
• The exile of Bahadur Shah Zafar was a symbolic end to the Mughal rule and the beginning of direct British governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance:**

 
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar is remembered as a tragic figure and a symbol of the end of Mughal sovereignty in India.
 
• His poetry, written during his exile, reflects his sorrow and longing for his homeland.
 
 
 
• **End of the Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• The deportation of Zafar to Rangoon marked the formal end of the Mughal dynasty, which had ruled parts of India for over three centuries.
 
• His death symbolized the consolidation of British authority in India.

questions.question: Which of the following coast lies in Karnataka and Kerala states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malabar Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Malabar Coast** is the coastal region that lies in the states of **Karnataka** and **Kerala**. It stretches along the western coastline of India and is known for its distinct geographical and cultural features.
 
• The coast is part of the **Western Ghats**, a UNESCO World Heritage site, making it an ecologically sensitive zone.
 
• It is characterized by a series of backwaters, lagoons, and rivers that make it a unique geographical feature. *Hence, Malabar Coast is the correct answer.*
 
• The coast has historical importance, as it was a major trade route for spices and other goods during ancient and medieval times. It was frequented by traders from **Arab countries, Europe, and China**.
 
• It is also famous for lush greenery, plantations of coconut and spices, and its unique cultural heritage, including classical dance forms like **Mohiniyattam** and **Kathakali**.
 
• The Malabar Coast is home to important cities such as **Kochi**, **Mangalore**, and **Kozhikode**, which are significant centers for tourism, trade, and culture.
 
• The coast is well known for its monsoon climate, which supports rich biodiversity and agricultural productivity. *Hence, the statement regarding the Malabar Coast being in Karnataka and Kerala is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Features:**

 
 
• The **Malabar Coast** is a narrow coastal plain flanked by the Western Ghats on the east and the Arabian Sea on the west.
 
• It includes a network of **backwaters** and canals, which are used for transportation, fishing, and tourism.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Malabar Coast was historically significant for its role in the **spice trade**, particularly for **pepper**, which earned the region the name "Pepper Coast".
 
• **Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama** landed at Kozhikode (Calicut) in **1498**, marking the beginning of European colonization in India.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• The Malabar Coast is part of the **Western Ghats**, which is a biodiversity hotspot hosting endemic species of flora and fauna.
 
• The region’s **backwaters** and wetlands provide habitat for numerous aquatic species and migratory birds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Coastal Regions in India:**

 
 
• **Kachchh Coast:** Located in Gujarat, this coast is famous for the **Rann of Kachchh**, a vast salt marsh.
 
• **Kathiawar Coast:** Lies in Gujarat and is known for its peninsular location and historical sites like **Somnath Temple**.
 
• **Konkan Coast:** Extends from Maharashtra to Karnataka and is characterized by rugged terrain, coastal villages, and ports like **Goa**.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Potential:**
 
 
• **Malabar Coast:** Famous for serene backwaters like **Alleppey** and houseboat cruises, attracting tourists globally.
 
• The region also hosts traditional festivals like **Onam** and offers culinary delights such as **Malabar biryani**.

questions.question: Manimekali, a notable work within early Tamil literature, is categorised as which type of literary composition?

__
 
• **Manimekalai** is one of the five great epics of early **Tamil literature**. It is considered a masterpiece and a significant work of Tamil literary tradition.
 
• This epic was composed by **Sithalai Sattanar**, a poet who lived during the Sangam age, around the 6th century CE.
 
• The story revolves around **Manimekalai**, the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, who chooses to follow the path of renunciation rather than pursuing worldly pleasures. *Hence, the work is categorized as an Epic.*
 
• The narrative embodies **Buddhist philosophy**, ethics, and teachings, showing the influence of Buddhism on Tamil culture and literature during its time.
 
• Manimekalai is a continuation of the epic **Silappadikaram**, another great Tamil epic, depicting the journey of Kovalan and Madhavi's lineage.
 
• Unlike autobiographies or treatises, which are generally factual and analytical, **Manimekalai** is a poetic work with a strong narrative and moral message, aligning with the characteristics of an epic.
 
• The work also highlights the **socio-cultural environment** of the Tamil region, including its values, religious practices, and philosophical outlook during its era. *Hence, the correct category for Manimekalai is Epic.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Epics in Tamil Literature:**

 
 
• **Manimekalai** is part of the **Five Great Epics** of Tamil literature, which includes Silappadikaram, Civaka Cintamani, Valayapathi, and Kundalakesi.
 
• Epics are long narrative poems that often depict heroic deeds, moral lessons, and cultural values. They serve as a mirror to the society and age in which they were composed.
 
 
 
• **Manimekalai’s Themes and Significance:**
 
 
• **Buddhism:** The epic is heavily influenced by Buddhist philosophy, focusing on themes of renunciation, compassion, and the pursuit of enlightenment.
 
• It critiques the caste system and advocates equality, highlighting the progressive thoughts of the time.
 
• The protagonist, **Manimekalai**, gains mystical powers and uses them to serve humanity, reflecting the importance of selflessness and altruism in Buddhist teachings.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Literary Categories:**
 
 
• **Autobiography:** An autobiography involves the self-narration of a person's life and experiences, which is not the case with Manimekalai.
 
• **Treatise:** Treatises are analytical works focused on a specific topic or argument, unlike the poetic and narrative style of Manimekalai.
 
• **Memoir:** Memoirs are personal accounts of specific events or periods, which again does not align with the epic nature of Manimekalai.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical and Cultural Context:**

 
 
• **Manimekalai** reflects the cultural and religious diversity of the Tamil region during the Sangam age, showcasing influences from Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism.
 
• It is a valuable resource for understanding the **social dynamics, ethical values, and philosophical outlook** of ancient Tamil society.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• As an epic, **Manimekalai** continues to be studied and revered for its literary excellence and its contribution to Tamil literature and philosophy.
 
• Its narrative style, philosophical depth, and moral lessons make it a timeless classic in the realm of world literature.

questions.question: The main objective of British economic policies in India was to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**benefit the British economy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary goal of British economic policies in India was to **serve the interests of the British economy**. The policies were designed to ensure maximum economic exploitation of India, benefiting Britain at the expense of Indian resources and economy.
 
• The British established a system where raw materials like **cotton, indigo, and jute** were sourced from India at cheap rates. These were then transported to Britain for processing into finished goods, which were sold back in India and other parts of the world at higher prices.
 
• The introduction of policies such as **land revenue systems** (e.g., Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems) and high taxes forced Indian farmers into poverty while ensuring a steady inflow of revenue to the British government. *This was aimed at benefiting the British economy.*
 
• The British discouraged Indian industries, especially traditional handicrafts and textiles, to promote British-manufactured goods. For example, the decline of the **Indian textile industry** was directly linked to the influx of British factory-made textiles. This was a deliberate move to create a dependent market for British exports.
 
• Indian railways, ports, and communication systems were developed primarily to facilitate the transport of raw materials to ports for export to Britain and to distribute imported British goods within India. These developments were not aimed at India's growth but rather at benefiting British trade. *This further highlights their economic motives.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of British Economic Policies on India:**

 
 
• **Deindustrialization:** India's traditional industries, such as handicrafts, collapsed due to competition from cheap, machine-made British goods. This led to widespread unemployment and a decline in artisanal skills.
 
• **Drain of Wealth:** A significant portion of India's wealth was transferred to Britain in the form of taxes, profits from British companies, and salaries paid to British officials. This concept was termed the **"Drain Theory"** by Dadabhai Naoroji.
 
• **Agrarian Distress:** Excessive taxation under land revenue systems and the focus on cash crops like indigo and cotton led to food shortages, famines, and a decline in the standard of living for Indian peasants.
 
• **Railway Network:** While the British established a railway network in India, it was primarily designed to transport raw materials to ports for export. It did little to benefit India's internal trade or economy.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Support rural employment:** This was not the aim of British economic policies. In fact, the decline of traditional industries and excessive taxation led to unemployment and poverty in rural areas.
 
• **Promote Indian self-sufficiency:** The British policies aimed at making India dependent on British goods and services. Self-sufficiency was actively discouraged to maintain economic dependency.
 
• **Industrialize India:** The British did not promote industrialization in India. Instead, they focused on using India as a supplier of raw materials and a market for British goods, leaving Indian industries to stagnate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory:** Propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji, it highlighted how India's wealth was systematically drained to Britain through unfair trade practices, taxes, and salaries of British officials.
 
• **Famines:** Excessive focus on cash crops and export-oriented agriculture led to frequent famines, with major famines occurring in 1770, 1876-78, and 1899-1900, causing the deaths of millions.
 
• **Examples of Exploitation:** The indigo plantations in Bengal and Bihar exploited Indian farmers, forcing them to grow indigo instead of food crops under oppressive conditions.
 
• **Decline in GDP:** India's share in the global GDP fell from about **23% in 1700** to less than **4% by 1950** due to British exploitation.

questions.question: Which of the following kings of Kalinga in the 2nd century B.C. professed Jainism in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kharavela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kharavela** was a prominent king of the Kalinga region in the 2nd century B.C. and one of the most famous rulers of the Mahameghavahana dynasty.
 
• He was a devout follower of **Jainism**, which significantly influenced his reign and policies.
 
• As per inscriptions such as the **Hathigumpha Inscription** in Udayagiri hills, Odisha, Kharavela patronized Jainism and worked to restore and promote it during his rule.
 
• He is credited with the revival of Jainism in Kalinga after it had declined due to the impact of Ashoka’s patronage of Buddhism.
 
• He undertook various public works to propagate Jainism, including the construction of Jain caves and temples, promoting the religion's teachings and practices.
 
• Kharavela's reign is noted for his efforts to spread peace and prosperity, as well as religious tolerance, while maintaining a strong focus on Jain principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kharavela:**

 
 
• Kharavela was a warrior-king as well as a patron of art, culture, and religion.
 
• The **Hathigumpha Inscription**, a significant source of information about him, details his military conquests, administrative policies, and religious endeavors.
 
• He constructed and renovated numerous Jain temples and monasteries, emphasizing his dedication to the Jain faith.
 
• Kharavela's reign is considered a golden period for Jainism in eastern India, particularly in Kalinga.
 
 
 
• **Jainism in Ancient India:**
 
 
• Jainism is an ancient religion originating in India, emphasizing non-violence, truth, and asceticism.
 
• During the 2nd century B.C., Jainism received patronage from rulers like Kharavela, helping it flourish alongside other religions such as Hinduism and Buddhism.
 
• Jainism's principles were spread through the construction of temples, caves, and inscriptions, many of which remain preserved today.
 
 
 
• **Other Kings Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Ashoka:** While Ashoka is famous for his adoption and propagation of Buddhism after the Kalinga War, there is no evidence that he professed Jainism.
 
• **Samprati:** He was a Mauryan king known for his patronage of Jainism, but he ruled in the 3rd century B.C., not in the 2nd century B.C.
 
• **Bindusara:** Bindusara, the father of Ashoka, was a follower of Ajivika, another ascetic religion, and did not profess Jainism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hathigumpha Inscription:**

 
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription, located in Odisha, is a 17-line inscription in the Brahmi script that provides a detailed account of Kharavela's reign.
 
• It highlights his military achievements, administrative reforms, and contributions to Jainism.
 
• This inscription is one of the earliest records of Jain kings in India.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance:**
 
 
• Kharavela is known for his religious tolerance, promoting Jainism while respecting other religious traditions.
 
• He encouraged cultural and artistic developments, enhancing the overall prosperity of his kingdom.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga:**
 
 
• Kalinga, located in present-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh, was a significant region in ancient India with a rich cultural and religious heritage.
 
• The region played an essential role in the history of Jainism and Buddhism due to its rulers' patronage.

questions.question: Each modern industrialised country, including India, has a National Metrology Institute (NMI). What is the main role of an NMI?

options.text: To regulate internet access in the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To maintain standards of measurements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Metrology Institute (NMI):** Every modern industrialized country, including **India**, has its own **National Metrology Institute** (NMI) responsible for maintaining the standards of measurement in the country.
 
• The primary role of an NMI is to establish, maintain, and disseminate **national measurement standards** that ensure consistency and accuracy in measurements across industries, research, trade, and daily life. Hence, the statement "To maintain standards of measurements" is correct.
 
• An NMI ensures **traceability**, which means connecting measurements to internationally recognized standards, improving global uniformity and trust in measurements and calibration. Hence, this is the correct answer.
 
• The statement "To monitor weather conditions" is incorrect as weather monitoring is done by meteorological departments (e.g., **India Meteorological Department**, IMD).
 
• The statement "To regulate internet access in the country" is incorrect as internet regulation is managed by communication and regulatory bodies such as **TRAI** (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India).
 
• The statement "To conduct medical research" is incorrect as medical research is carried out by health departments, research institutions, and bodies such as the **Indian Council of Medical Research** (ICMR).
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is To maintain standards of measurements.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of National Metrology Institute (NMI):**

 
 
• An NMI develops and maintains **primary measurement standards** that serve as the highest reference point for measurements within the nation.
 
• It ensures **accuracy and uniformity** of measurements, which are critical for industrial production, scientific research, and international trade.
 
• In India, the **National Physical Laboratory (NPL)** serves as the NMI and oversees the **calibration and dissemination** of measurement standards.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Standards Maintained:**
 
 
• Standards for **mass, length, temperature, time, electrical measurements**, and other physical quantities.
 
• For instance, the NPL maintains the **Indian standard for the kilogram** and ensures it aligns with the **International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM)**.
 
 
 
• **International Cooperation:**
 
 
• NMIs collaborate globally to ensure **international traceability**, enabling seamless trade and scientific advancements.
 
• India's NPL works in coordination with other NMIs and participates in the activities of **BIPM**, the **International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML)**, and other international bodies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal and Organizational Framework:**

 
 
• The NPL, India's NMI, operates under the **CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research)** and provides calibration services to industries, laboratories, and other institutions.
 
• The **Weights and Measures Act** governs the use of standardized measurements in India to ensure consistency in trade and industry.
 
 
 
• **Global Importance of NMIs:**
 
 
• NMIs are vital for ensuring **precision and reliability** in measurements, which are crucial for modern technological advancements, industrial production, and scientific research.
 
• For example, the role of NMIs was critical in redefining the **kilogram** in 2019 based on the **Planck constant** to improve measurement accuracy worldwide.

questions.question: Colonial policies significantly altered India’s trade structure. Which of the following best describes India’s foreign trade pattern at the time of independence?

options.text: Export of capital goods and import of consumer goods
Export of finished goods and import of raw materials
Balanced trade between agriculture and industry
Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **colonial period**, British policies were designed to suit their industrial and economic interests in England, which significantly affected India's trade structure.
 
• The primary focus was on making India a supplier of **raw materials** for British industries and a market for their **manufactured goods**. This disrupted India's self-sustaining economy.
 
• At the time of independence in **1947**, India's trade pattern was structured such that the country mainly exported **raw materials** like cotton, jute, and indigo.
 
• Simultaneously, India imported large quantities of **manufactured goods**, particularly textiles and machinery, from Britain. This led to a dependency on British goods and a decline in Indian handicrafts and industries.
 
• The policy of exporting raw materials and importing manufactured goods left India with a trade deficit and a weak industrial base, which persisted at the time of independence.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Colonial Impact on India’s Trade:**

 
 
• Colonial policies transformed India into an **agrarian economy** focused on producing cash crops like cotton, tea, and jute for export, rather than food crops for domestic consumption.
 
• The export of raw materials such as **cotton, jute, and indigo** was heavily promoted to feed Britain's industrial revolution.
 
• India became a significant importer of British-manufactured goods, especially textiles, as traditional Indian industries were deliberately suppressed through policies like high tariffs on Indian exports.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Trade Pattern at Independence:**
 
 
• India's trade structure was highly imbalanced, with a focus on **primary goods** exports and **finished goods** imports.
 
• This led to a lack of diversification in the economy and made India dependent on foreign goods for industrial and consumer needs.
 
 
 
• **Role of British Policies:**
 
 
• The **Drain of Wealth Theory**, as proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, highlighted how wealth was systematically drained from India by the British through such trade patterns.
 
• Heavy taxes on Indian manufacturers and incentives for British imports ensured the collapse of Indian industries.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• **Textile Industry:** India, once a leading exporter of textiles, became an importer of British-manufactured textiles due to policies that discouraged domestic production.
 
• **Indigo:** Indigo plantations were set up to meet the demand for dyes in Britain, often at the expense of Indian farmers' livelihoods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** Export of capital goods and import of consumer goods – This is incorrect as India did not focus on capital goods production during the colonial period.
 
• **Option 2:** Export of finished goods and import of raw materials – This is incorrect as India exported raw materials and imported finished goods, not the other way around.
 
• **Option 3:** Balanced trade between agriculture and industry – This is incorrect as trade was highly imbalanced, favoring British interests.
 
• **Option 4:** Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods – This is the correct answer as it aligns with India's trade pattern during British rule.
 
 
 
• **Economic Consequences:**
 
 
• Colonial trade policies led to **deindustrialization** in India, with traditional industries declining and a lack of modern industrial development.
 
• India's dependence on agriculture increased, but without adequate focus on productivity or diversification.

questions.question: Which British policy promoted English education to create a loyal class serving British interests in India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Education Policy** introduced by the British in India aimed at promoting English education to create a class of Indians who would assist in administrative functions and remain loyal to British interests.
 
• Lord Macaulay, in his famous **Minute on Indian Education** (1835), advocated English as the medium of instruction, stating that it would help create a class of people who were "Indian in blood and color but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect."
 
• The objective of this policy was to produce a small group of educated Indians who could act as intermediaries between the British rulers and the Indian masses and support colonial governance. *Hence, the option "Education Policy" is correct.*
 
• By promoting English education, the British also aimed to suppress indigenous learning systems and create a dependency on Western knowledge and culture.
 
• This policy led to the establishment of schools, colleges, and universities where English was the primary language of instruction, such as the **University of Calcutta** (1857).
 
• The promotion of English education also laid the foundation for India's intellectual awakening, which ultimately contributed to the rise of nationalist movements. *Hence, the statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance** was a strategic political and military policy introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, the Governor-General of India (1798–1805).
 
• It required Indian princely states to accept British forces within their territory and pay for their maintenance, effectively reducing their independence.
 
 
 
• **Divide and Rule Policy:**
 
 
• The **Divide and Rule** policy aimed to create divisions among various religious, social, and ethnic groups in India to weaken unity and maintain British control.
 
• This policy was prominently used during the partition of Bengal in **1905** and later during the partition of India in **1947**.
 
 
 
• **Trade Policy:**
 
 
• The British trade policy focused on exploiting India's resources and turning it into a market for British goods, leading to the deindustrialization of Indian handicrafts and industries.
 
• India was transformed into an agrarian economy, and the export of raw materials like cotton and jute increased significantly under colonial rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of British Education Policy:**

 
 
• The introduction of English education led to the emergence of a middle class in India, which became influential in socio-political reforms and the freedom struggle.
 
• While it created opportunities for Indians to access modern Western knowledge, it also eroded traditional systems of education and culture.
 
 
 
• **Key Developments:**
 
 
• **1835:** Lord Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education advocated the promotion of English and Western education.
 
• **1854:** Wood’s Dispatch emphasized the need for establishing universities and improving education infrastructure in India.
 
• **1857:** Universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras were established as centers of higher education.

questions.question: Tussocky grass grows mainly in which type of forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Thorn Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tussocky grass** refers to a type of grass that grows in clumps or tufts, often found in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
• **Tropical Thorn Forests** are characterized by their dry conditions and sparse vegetation. These forests predominantly occur in regions with low rainfall, typically below 70 cm annually.
 
• The vegetation in these forests consists of thorny bushes, scattered trees, and a significant presence of tussocky grass, which is well-adapted to dry climates and poor soil conditions. *Hence, the correct answer is Tropical Thorn Forests.*
 
• These forests are typically found in regions such as parts of **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, and the Deccan Plateau** in India.
 
• The tussocky grass in these forests provides essential forage for grazing animals, which is crucial for the pastoral economy of the local population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tropical Thorn Forests:**

 
 
• These forests are found in regions with **low rainfall (below 70 cm annually)** and extreme temperatures ranging from very hot summers to cold winters.
 
• The vegetation is sparse and consists of **thorny plants and scattered trees** such as acacias, euphorbias, and palms. These plants are adapted to conserve water in dry conditions.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Tussocky Grass:**
 
 
• It is a type of perennial grass that grows in small clumps or tufts, making it well-suited to arid and semi-arid environments.
 
• The grass is drought-resistant and can survive in poor soil conditions, making it a crucial plant species in tropical thorn forests.
 
• **Example:** Species like **Chrysopogon fulvus** and **Cenchrus ciliaris** are commonly found tussocky grasses in these regions.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Forests in the Options:**
 
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests:** Found in regions with moderate rainfall (70-200 cm), these forests shed their leaves during the dry season. They are characterized by trees such as sal, teak, and mahua.
 
• **Evergreen Forests:** Found in regions with heavy rainfall (over 200 cm), these forests are dense and remain green throughout the year. They contain trees like mahogany, ebony, and rosewood.
 
• **Montane Forests:** Found in mountainous regions, these forests vary depending on altitude. They include species like deodars, pines, and firs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Adaptations of Vegetation in Tropical Thorn Forests:**

• **Natural Gas Transport Fuel:** While natural gas is considered a relatively cleaner fossil fuel compared to coal and oil, its combustion still produces **carbon dioxide (CO2)**, a major greenhouse gas. Additionally, methane leaks during production and transport exacerbate its greenhouse gas footprint. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Thermal Power Plants:** Thermal power plants burn fossil fuels such as coal, natural gas, or oil to generate electricity. This process releases significant amounts of greenhouse gases like **CO2** and **nitrous oxide**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• **Diesel Generators:** Diesel generators are widely used for backup power but emit greenhouse gases during operation due to the combustion of diesel. __
 
• **Tidal Energy:**

 
 
• Tidal energy is harnessed using tidal barrages, tidal streams, or tidal lagoons. These systems convert the energy of moving water into electricity using turbines.

• **Example:** The La Rance Tidal Power Station in **France** is one of the oldest tidal power stations, showcasing the efficiency of this clean energy source.
 
 
 
• **Natural Gas Transport Fuel:**

• **Methane Leaks:** Methane, the primary component of natural gas, is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential approximately **25 times higher than CO2**.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Power Plants:**
 
 
• Thermal power plants are one of the largest sources of greenhouse gas emissions globally, primarily due to the burning of fossil fuels.
 
• Coal-fired power plants release substantial amounts of **CO2**, as well as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, which contribute to acid rain and air pollution.
 
• **Example:** The United States and China are among the largest producers of electricity from thermal power plants.
 
 
 
• **Diesel Generators:**
 
 
• Diesel generators are used in areas with unreliable electricity supply or during power outages. However, they are inefficient and contribute heavily to greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• **Particulate Matter:** In addition to GHG emissions, diesel generators release particulate matter, which poses health risks such as respiratory and cardiovascular issues.

• **Global Examples of Tidal Energy:**
 
 
• **South Korea:** The Sihwa Lake Tidal Power Plant is the largest tidal energy installation globally, producing **254 MW**.

questions.question: Which of the following options best represents the predictions of a Punnett square?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genotype and phenotype probabilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Punnett Square:** A Punnett square is a diagram that is used to predict the possible **genotypes** and **phenotypes** of offspring resulting from a genetic cross between two parents. It is especially useful in studying inheritance patterns.
 
• **Genotype Probabilities:** It helps calculate the likelihood of specific genetic combinations (e.g., homozygous dominant, homozygous recessive, or heterozygous) in the offspring. This feature is one of the key predictions of the Punnett square.
 
• **Phenotype Probabilities:** Based on the genotypes, the Punnett square also determines the chances of physical traits (phenotypes) being expressed in the offspring. For example, dominant traits might be expressed more frequently than recessive ones.
 
• **Example:** In a monohybrid cross, if one parent is heterozygous (Aa) and the other is homozygous recessive (aa), the Punnett square will show the probabilities of offspring being Aa (50%) or aa (50%), which also corresponds to the phenotypic expression of the dominant or recessive trait.
 
• **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
 
 
• **Genetic linkage relationships in siblings:** Punnett squares do not study genetic linkage, which refers to genes located close together on a chromosome that are inherited together.
 
• **Genetic mutations over several generations:** The Punnett square does not track mutations or predict their occurrence over generations; it only deals with existing alleles.
 
• **DNA sequence in parents:** Punnett squares do not analyze the DNA sequence directly but focus on the inheritance of alleles and traits.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Applications of Punnett Square:**

 
 
• It is widely used in **Mendelian genetics** to study monohybrid and dihybrid crosses.
 
• Helps predict the probability of inheriting genetic diseases like **sickle cell anemia** or **cystic fibrosis**.
 
• Used in breeding programs to select for desired traits in plants and animals.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Punnett Square:**
 
 
• It assumes that genes assort independently, which may not be true in cases of **genetic linkage.**
 
• It does not account for **polygenic traits** (traits controlled by multiple genes) or environmental influences.
 
 
 
• **Terms Related to the Punnett Square:**
 
 
• **Homozygous:** An individual with two identical alleles for a trait (e.g., AA or aa).
 
• **Heterozygous:** An individual with two different alleles for a trait (e.g., Aa).
 
• **Dominant allele:** An allele that masks the expression of a recessive allele in a heterozygous individual.
 
• **Recessive allele:** An allele that is only expressed when two copies are present (homozygous recessive).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History:** The Punnett square was devised by **Reginald C. Punnett**, a British geneticist, in the early 20th century as part of Mendelian genetics.
 
• **Mendel’s Laws:** The Punnett square is based on two key principles:
 
 
• **Law of Segregation:** Each parent contributes one allele for a trait to the offspring.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment:** Genes for different traits are inherited independently (if unlinked).
 
 
 
• **Modern Use:** While the Punnett square is simple, it forms the foundation for more advanced genetic studies, including **probabilistic modeling** and **population genetics.**

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act abolished the provision for nominating members from the Anglo-Indian community to the State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**104th Amendment Act, 2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **104th Amendment Act, 2019** abolished the provision for nominating members from the **Anglo-Indian community** to the **State Legislative Assemblies** and the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• Before the amendment, under **Article 331** and **Article 333** of the Indian Constitution, the President and Governors could nominate two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, respectively.
 
• The **Anglo-Indian community** was provided this representation as they were considered a minority group with unique cultural and historical significance in India.
 
• The **104th Amendment Act** repealed this provision, as it was deemed that the Anglo-Indian community had integrated well into Indian society and no longer needed reserved representation in legislative bodies.
 
• This amendment is significant as it reflects the evolving approach of the Indian Constitution to the representation of minority communities in legislative institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anglo-Indian Community:**

 
 
• The term **Anglo-Indian** refers to people of mixed Indian and European ancestry. This group played an important role during British rule in India.
 
• Historically, the Anglo-Indian community worked in the railways, education, and government services. They had a distinct identity and were given reserved representation post-Independence to safeguard their interests.
 
 
 
• **Articles Related to Anglo-Indian Reservation:**
 
 
• **Article 331:** Allowed the President to nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha if he/she felt that the community was not adequately represented.
 
• **Article 333:** Allowed Governors to nominate one member of the Anglo-Indian community to the State Legislative Assembly under the same conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Features of the 104th Amendment Act:**
 
 
• The amendment extended the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another 10 years, until **2030**.
 
• While the reservation for SCs and STs was extended, the provision for Anglo-Indian representation was abolished as it was considered no longer necessary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• **104th Constitutional Amendment Act** was passed by the Parliament in **December 2019** and came into effect on **January 25, 2020**.
 
• The amendment required a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament and was supported across party lines.
 
 
 
• **Other Constitutional Amendments Related to Elections:**
 
 
• **101st Amendment Act, 2016:** Introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, which is unrelated to the topic of representation.
 
• **102nd Amendment Act, 2018:** Gave constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)**.
 
• **105th Amendment Act, 2021:** Restored the power of states to identify and notify **Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs)**.

questions.question: Which of the following films is considered the first Indian sound (talkie) film, marking the beginning of Bollywood?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alam Ara (1931)** was the **first Indian sound film**, marking the beginning of the "talkie" era in Indian cinema.
 
• Directed by **Ardeshir Irani**, Alam Ara was released on **14 March 1931**. It was a milestone in Indian cinema and paved the way for the Bollywood industry.
 
• The film featured dialogue and songs, making it revolutionary compared to silent movies that existed before. *Hence, Alam Ara is considered the first Indian talkie film.*
 
• **Raja Harishchandra**, made by **Dadasaheb Phalke** in 1913, was India's first full-length silent feature film. It does not qualify as the first sound film. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Sholay** (1975) and **Mughal-e-Azam** (1960) were significant films in Indian cinema but were not the first sound films. *Hence, statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.*
 
• Alam Ara featured seven songs and introduced playback singing in Indian cinema. The song **"De de khuda ke naam par"** sung by **Wazir Mohammed Khan** became iconic.
 
• The film's themes revolved around **royal intrigue, love, and family drama**, setting a precedent for Bollywood's storytelling style. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alam Ara:**

 
 
• **Production:** Alam Ara was produced by **Imperial Movietone**. Ardeshir Irani used the **Tantra system** to record sound, which was cutting-edge technology at the time.
 
• **Plot:** The story revolved around a love triangle between a prince, a gypsy girl, and a princess. It included themes of **romance, betrayal, and conflict.**
 
• **Impact:** Alam Ara inspired the production of sound films across India, creating a shift from silent cinema to talkies.
 
 
 
• **Raja Harishchandra:**
 
 
• **Directed by:** Dadasaheb Phalke, considered the "Father of Indian Cinema".
 
• **Release:** 1913, it marked the beginning of Indian cinema but was a **silent film**.
 
• **Significance:** It laid the foundation for India's film industry but did not feature sound.
 
 
 
• **Sound in Indian Cinema:**
 
 
• The advent of sound films brought new opportunities for Indian cinema, including **dialogue, playback singing, and sound effects**.
 
• **Example:** Alam Ara set the tone for Bollywood's musical and dramatic themes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Advancements:**

 
 
• **Sound Recording:** Alam Ara was recorded using the Tanar system, which was the first sound recording technology used in India.
 
• **Playback Singing:** The concept of playback singing was introduced, which later became a hallmark of Indian cinema.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Alam Ara:**
 
 
• The film is no longer available as the **prints of Alam Ara were destroyed**. However, it remains a crucial part of Indian cinematic history.
 
• **Recognition:** Alam Ara is remembered as the first Indian sound film, a pioneer in integrating sound and storytelling.

questions.question: Which of the following is the function of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) in a computer?

options.text: It receives input from the keyboard and mouse only
It stores all user files permanently.
It processes data and controls operations of all parts of the computer.
It sends output to printers and monitors.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It processes data and controls operations of all parts of the computer.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** is often referred to as the "brain" of the computer because it is responsible for carrying out critical functions such as executing instructions and managing system operations.
 
• The primary function of the CPU is to **process data and control operations** of all parts of the computer. It ensures that the input from the user is processed and the desired output is generated. *Hence, this is correct.*
 
• The CPU does not store user files permanently. That function is performed by storage devices like the hard disk or SSD. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• While the CPU receives input from devices such as the keyboard and mouse, it is not limited to these devices. It processes input from other peripherals as well, such as scanners and microphones. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• The CPU does not directly send output to printers and monitors; it processes the data that is then sent to these output devices via other components like the GPU or I/O controllers. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of the CPU:**

 
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):** Responsible for performing arithmetic operations (e.g., addition, subtraction) and logical operations (e.g., comparisons).
 
• **Control Unit (CU):** Manages the execution of instructions by directing the flow of data and coordinating between the CPU and other components of the system.
 
• **Registers:** Small, high-speed storage locations within the CPU that temporarily hold data and instructions during processing.
 
 
 
• **CPU Operations:**
 
 
• **Fetch:** The CPU retrieves instructions from memory.
 
• **Decode:** The CPU interprets the instructions to determine the operation to be performed.
 
• **Execute:** The CPU performs the operation, such as calculations or data transfer.
 
 
 
• **Examples of CPUs:**
 
 
• **Intel Core:** A popular CPU series for desktops and laptops.
 
• **AMD Ryzen:** Known for offering high performance at competitive prices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CPU Performance Factors:**

 
 
• **Clock Speed:** Measured in GHz, it determines how many cycles a CPU can perform per second.
 
• **Core Count:** Multiple cores allow a CPU to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.
 
• **Cache Memory:** High-speed memory that stores frequently accessed data to improve performance.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Used in personal computers, servers, and embedded systems like smartphones and IoT devices.
 
• Specialized CPUs like GPUs are used for tasks like gaming, video editing, and AI computations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of India’s federal system, thereby reflecting its unitary character?

options.text: Single citizenship for the entire country
Requirement of some Constitutional Amendments to be ratified by States
An upper house of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) representing the states
Division of powers between the Centre and States

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Single citizenship for the entire country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India follows a **single citizenship** system, meaning that all Indian citizens are recognized as citizens of India regardless of the state or territory they belong to. This ensures unity across the country and reflects the **unitary character** of the Indian Constitution. *Hence, this feature is NOT federal and is unitary in nature.*
 
• The requirement of certain **Constitutional Amendments** to be ratified by the states is a federal feature. Such provisions ensure the participation of states in the amendment process, protecting the federal balance. *Hence, this statement reflects federalism.*
 
• The existence of an **upper house of Parliament, the Rajya Sabha**, representing the states is a distinct federal feature. Rajya Sabha members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states, ensuring state representation at the central level. *Hence, this statement reflects federalism.*
 
• The **division of powers** between the Centre and the States is the cornerstone of federalism in India. It is implemented through the division of subjects in the Union, State, and Concurrent Lists under the Constitution. *Hence, this statement reflects federalism.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Single Citizenship:**

 
 
• Unlike countries like the United States or Canada, where citizens hold dual citizenship at the national and state/provincial levels, India provides **single citizenship**. This ensures that every citizen is recognized uniformly under Indian law.
 
• The provision of single citizenship is enshrined in **Part II of the Indian Constitution (Articles 5-11)**. It avoids complexities in legal and administrative matters and promotes the idea of national unity.
 
 
 
• **Federal Features:**
 
 
• India's federal structure includes features such as the **division of powers** between the Centre and states, a written Constitution, an independent judiciary, and bicameralism with the Rajya Sabha representing the states.
 
• However, the federal system in India is not absolute. It is described as a "quasi-federal" system with a strong tilt toward centralization. This is evident in provisions like single citizenship.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples of Federal Features:**
 
 
• The **73rd and 74th Amendments** introduced local self-government institutions (Panchayats and Municipalities), reflecting India's decentralized governance model.
 
• The role of the **Finance Commission** in recommending financial allocations between the Centre and states is another key federal feature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unitary Features of Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution incorporates several unitary features like **single citizenship, a unified judiciary, and the authority of the Union over states during emergencies**. These features centralize power and ensure national integrity.
 
• During national emergencies under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**, India's federal structure transforms into a more unitary system, with significant powers vested in the Centre.
 
 
 
• **Key Developments:**
 
 
• The single citizenship provision has helped maintain India's unity and prevent regionalism, ensuring that all citizens enjoy equal rights across the country irrespective of their state or territory.
 
• This feature has been significant in avoiding legal complexities that could arise from dual citizenship systems, as seen in other federal nations like the United States.

• **Panama** became the first **Latin American country** to withdraw from **China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** in **February 2025**. This marked a significant geopolitical shift in the region's relationship with China.
 
• The **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** is China's global development strategy aimed at infrastructure and investment projects across the globe, involving nearly 150 countries and international organizations.

• **Eleventh Schedule:** The **Eleventh Schedule** was introduced in the **Constitution of India** by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**. It contains a list of **29 subjects** that have been allocated to the **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**.
 
• These subjects are meant to decentralize the power and ensure **local self-governance** at the village and rural levels.
 
• The subjects include matters like **agriculture, irrigation, rural housing, rural electrification, education, health, and sanitation**, among others. These functions are intended to empower the grassroots governance system. *Hence, the correct answer is Panchayati Raj Institutions.*
 
• The **objective** of the Eleventh Schedule is to enhance participation in governance by bringing decision-making closer to the people and ensuring development at the local level.

• The **Panchayati Raj system** in India is a three-tier system of governance at the village, block, and district levels. It was institutionalized through the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**.
 
• It aims to promote **democratic decentralization** and ensure governance at the grassroots level by empowering elected local bodies.
 
 
 
• **Subjects under the Eleventh Schedule:**
 
 
• The 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule include critical areas such as **agriculture, water management, health, education, rural housing, social welfare, and poverty alleviation programs**.
 
• These subjects ensure that Panchayati Raj Institutions have the authority to address **local needs and concerns** effectively.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The **Article 243G** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Panchayati Raj Institutions to function as units of self-governance and take decisions on these subjects.
 
• This provision ensures that the local bodies have the authority to plan and implement schemes for **economic development and social justice**.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation 'PCB' stand for in operating systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Process Control Block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Process Control Block (PCB)** is a data structure used by the operating system to store all information about a process. It is crucial for process management and scheduling.
 
• The PCB contains several fields, including **process state**, **program counter**, **CPU registers**, **memory management information**, and **I/O status information**. These fields are vital for the operating system to manage processes efficiently.
 
• The **process state field** records the current state of a process, such as ready, running, waiting, or terminated. It allows the system to determine the next action for the process.
 
• The **program counter field** holds the address of the next instruction to be executed for the process. This ensures that the process resumes correctly after an interruption.
 
• The **CPU registers field** stores the values of the process's registers when it is not executing. This enables the process to resume execution without losing its state.
 
• The **memory management information** includes details about the memory allocated to the process, such as base and limit registers, page tables, and segment tables. This ensures proper memory access and protection.
 
• The **I/O status information field** tracks the I/O devices allocated to the process and its status. It helps the operating system manage I/O operations effectively.
 
• The PCB enables **context switching**, which is the process of saving the state of a currently running process and restoring the state of another process. This ensures multitasking and system efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Process Control Block:**

 
 
• The PCB is crucial for **process scheduling**, as it allows the operating system to determine which process should run next based on its priority and state.
 
• It facilitates **inter-process communication** (IPC) by storing information about the resources shared among processes.
 
• The PCB helps in **process synchronization**, ensuring that processes do not conflict when accessing shared resources.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Program Control Block:** This is incorrect as no such term exists in the context of operating systems. It may be confused with the Process Control Block.
 
• **Primary Communication Bus:** This term refers to the hardware bus system used for data transfer among components in a computer. It is unrelated to the process management functionality of an operating system.
 
• **Process Communication Block:** While this term may seem plausible, it is not a standard term in operating system terminology. Process communication is handled by IPC mechanisms, not by a separate block named Process Communication Block.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Components of PCB:**

 
 
• The PCB contains **process identification** information, such as process ID, parent process ID, and user ID. This helps the operating system uniquely identify and manage processes.
 
• The **process priority field** determines the priority of a process for scheduling purposes. Higher-priority processes are executed before lower-priority ones.
 
• The PCB also includes **accounting information**, such as CPU usage, time limits, and job or process numbers. This data is essential for resource utilization tracking and billing in multi-user systems.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• The PCB is used in **multitasking systems** to ensure seamless switching between processes. For example, in a multitasking operating system like **Linux**, the PCB is essential for efficient process management.
 
• In **real-time operating systems (RTOS)**, the PCB plays a crucial role in maintaining process deadlines and ensuring timely task execution.

questions.question: If the 6-digit number N84M69 is divisible by 11, then which of the options below can give a possible correct relation between M and N?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by 11, the difference between the sums of alternate digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Sum of digits at odd places = N + 4 + 6 = N + 10

Sum of digits at even places = 8 + M + 9 = M + 17

Difference = (M + 17) − (N + 10) = M − N + 7

Equating the difference to 0 gives: M − N + 7 = 0 ⇒ M − N = −7

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = −7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 6-digit number is N84M69.

The number is completely divisible by 11.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference of the alternating sum of its digits is exactly 0 or a multiple of 11 (such as 11, 22, -11).

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum of digits at odd positions (from left) = N + 4 + 6 = N + 10

⇒ Sum of digits at even positions (from left) = 8 + M + 9 = M + 17

⇒ Difference between the two sums = (M + 17) − (N + 10)

⇒ Difference = M − N + 7

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 11, M − N + 7 = 0, 11, 22, etc.

⇒ Case 1: M − N + 7 = 0 ⇒ M − N = −7

⇒ Case 2: M − N + 7 = 11 ⇒ M − N = 4

⇒ Checking the given options, the relation M − N = −7 is available as a valid relation.

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = −7.**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is completely divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11 and 13

A large number is divisible by 7, 11, or 13 if the alternating difference of blocks of three digits starting from right to left is a multiple of 7, 11, or 13.

questions.question: Which of the following is the greatest number that, when dividing 183, 127 and 211, leaves the same remainder each time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number leaving the same remainder is the HCF of their absolute differences.

Differences = |183 − 127|, |211 − 127|, |211 − 183|

Differences = 56, 84, 28

Required Number = HCF(56, 84, 28) = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 183, 127, and 211.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number that will divide x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case is given by the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference 1 = |183 − 127| = 56

⇒ Difference 2 = |127 − 211| = 84

⇒ Difference 3 = |211 − 183| = 28

⇒ Now, we need to find the HCF of 56, 84, and 28.

⇒ Factors of 28 = 2 × 2 × 7

⇒ Factors of 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7

⇒ Factors of 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ The common factors are 2, 2, and 7.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 2 × 7 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest number leaving specific remainders

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively is the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Smallest number leaving the same remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is LCM(x, y, z) + r.

LCM and HCF Relation

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.
</p

questions.question: The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 182. The greater of the two numbers is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two consecutive natural numbers, their product is close to the square of either number.

The consecutive natural numbers closest to 13.49 are 13 and 14.

Since 13 × 14 = 182, the two numbers are indeed 13 and 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**Given:**

The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 182.

**Method Used:**

Let the two consecutive natural numbers be x and (x + 1).

**Calculations:**

⇒ x(x + 1) = 182

⇒ x² + x = 182

⇒ x² + x − 182 = 0

⇒ x² + 14x − 13x − 182 = 0

⇒ x(x + 14) − 13(x + 14) = 0

⇒ The given numbers are: 306, 307, 308, 309, 310, 311, 312, 313.

⇒ Eliminate the even numbers (306, 308, 310, 312) directly as they are divisible by 2.

⇒ The remaining odd numbers to check are: 307, 309, 311, 313.

⇒ 311: Not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, or 17 → Prime.

Prime Number Test

To rapidly check if a large number N is prime, find its approximate square root √N. Test its divisibility using only the prime numbers up to √N. If N is not divisible by any of them, it is a prime number.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3. This is an essential check to eliminate non-primes quickly. For instance, 309 has a digit sum of 12, marking it as a composite number.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers divides 3,27,087?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the divisibility rule of 3, a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

Sum of digits of 3,27,087 = 3 + 2 + 7 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 27.

Since 27 is perfectly divisible by 3, the entire number is also divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The number to be checked is 3,27,087.

**Method Used:**

We apply standard divisibility rules for each given option to find the exact divisor.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **For 12:** A number must be divisible by both 3 and 4. The last two digits (87) are odd and not divisible by 4. So, it is not divisible by 12.

⇒ **For 8:** Any number divisible by 8 must be an even number. Since 3,27,087 ends in 7, it is odd and cannot be divisible by 8.

⇒ **For 5:** A number is divisible by 5 only if its last digit is 0 or 5. Here, the last digit is 7, so it is not divisible by 5.

⇒ **For 3:** The sum of the digits = 3 + 2 + 7 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 27.

⇒ As 27 is divisible by 3, the given number 3,27,087 is perfectly divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

Similar to the rule of 3, a number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its individual digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is either 0 or perfectly divisible by 11.
